title: Maximum Points Inside the Square
summary: Given a 2D array of points and their tags, find the maximum number of points that can form a square centered at the origin with edges parallel to the axes, where no two points share the same tag.
statement: Given a 2D array of points and their tags, find the maximum number of points that can form a square centered at the origin with edges parallel to the axes, where no two points share the same tag.
constraints: points and s have equal nonzero length, with one tag character per point.
A centered axis-aligned square of radius d contains exactly points with max(abs(x),abs(y))≤d.
Maximize contained points subject to all contained tags being distinct.
hints: All points at the same Chebyshev distance enter a centered square simultaneously.
Group by max absolute coordinate, process distances together, and stop before the first group that duplicates a tag internally or previously seen.
At each sorted distance collect tags; if group has duplicates or intersects seen, return prior count; otherwise add all.
Every possible contained set changes only at a group boundary, and the first duplicate can never be removed by enlarging the square.
editorial: Every possible contained set changes only at a group boundary, and the first duplicate can never be removed by enlarging the square.

tests.explanation: Radius two contains the first two points with distinct tags; the next distance introduces a repeated a, so the maximum is two.
All three tags are distinct, so a radius-two square contains all points.
